chunks: God has not provided two hearts in the breast of a man, nor made your wives, whom you pronounce "mothers" (in order to divorce them), your real mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your real sons. This is only what your lips pronounce. God says what is just, and shows the right way.

key_terms.تُظَاهِرُونَ: You pronounce Zihar (divorce by equating wife to mother)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Zihar and adoption in Islam according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Ahzab (33:4) establishes the theological principle of divine unity in human nature while abrogating pre-Islamic customs regarding Zihar and adoption, a key moment in the transition from tribal to Islamic family structures. Shia scholars emphasize that 'two hearts' refers to the capacity for dual loyalty or distinct spiritual states, while the legal rulings on adopted sons (like Zayd ibn Harithah) underscore that lineage is biological, not merely declarative. The verse concludes by contrasting human verbal assertions with God's absolute truth, reinforcing the authority of divine revelation over cultural tradition.
